issue: The record has no description, so the five group codes (EDG, CEDG, LMG, CLMG, VG) are undocumented. They are kept verbatim.
UserStudy.csv is not valid UTF-8 (timestamps contain mis-encoded CJK characters); it is read as latin-1 and only numeric/ASCII columns are used.
P16CLMG.csv ends with 394 rows whose sensor columns are empty; they are dropped.
Trial 1 includes any idle time before the participant started moving.
The description names four conditions, but the workbook has a fifth sheet (NoEucDoble) that is not described.
The description mentions 10 Hz tracking logs, but the record only contains the summary workbook.
Four participant-condition rows are empty (U07 Euc, U08 EucCol, U33 NoEucCol, U31 NoEucDoble) and are dropped.
Each sheet ends with one or two unlabeled mean rows; they are dropped.
Condition order per participant is not recorded, so learning effects cannot be separated from condition effects.
No age or gender is recorded; only academic group (UG, PG, PhD).
63 of 190 durations are whole minutes (about 3 would be expected by chance), so some start and end times were probably recorded to the minute.

33 conventional tasks are marked Success_0_1 = 1 (correct book retrieved) but Accuracy_Score_0_3 = 0 (wrong rack, side and shelf). Both columns are kept as given; outcome_errors comes from the accuracy score.
The data dictionary lists Route_Deviation_m, which is not in the data, and allows User_Group "UG / PhD", but 20 participants are "PG".
The description reports 129 respondents and 5,772 ratings; the file contains 122 respondents and 5,771 ratings.
12 respondents have fewer than the expected 48 ratings (one has only 13).

The README age coding (1 = under 18, 2 = 18-30, ...) contradicts the file's own `young` flag, which marks every code-1 respondent as under 30. The codes are mapped one step down (1 = 18-30), and a test checks that the mapping agrees with `young`.
The README lists code 3 twice (31-40 and 41-50) and calls the e-scooter mode `escooter`, while the file uses `escoot`.
